key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that about 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while increasing its band gap.
engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial design of perovskite solar absorbers where static calculations miss dynamic structural and electronic responses.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors.
Track lattice symmetry, octahedral tilts, molecular orientations, and snapshot-averaged band gaps.
evidence_signal: The predicted transition and tensile-strain band-gap blue shift agree with reported experiments, while bulk and slab models show consistent trends.
watch_item: Predictions concern MAPbI₃ at 300 K; applicability to other compositions, temperatures, or explicit substrate interfaces requires validation.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
